title: Claude Code's Permission Sandbox: Four Escapes Closed in Five Days
caption:
Four Claude Code releases in five days, every one of them closing a permission-sandbox hole.

Tabs and invisible Unicode kept part of a command out of the approval dialog you clicked (2.1.223). A zsh [[ ]] regex conditional ran commands the Bash permission check never saw (2.1.221). Worktree-isolated sessions could still run destructive git against the main checkout (2.1.222). And denyRead "~/.aws/" was silently bypassable because of the trailing slash (2.1.224).

If you hand an agent permissions, the fence is only as good as the version you are on.

What version are you on?

slides.title: Five days, four releases
items: 2.1.222 (Aug 4) worktree isolation missed git and hooks
2.1.223 (Aug 5) tabs and invisible Unicode hid commands

slides.title: Padding hid the command
slides.sub: Tabs or invisible Unicode kept part of a command out of the approval dialog you clicked. Fixed in 2.1.223.

slides.title: zsh ran hidden commands
slides.sub: A [[ ]] regex conditional could execute commands the Bash permission check never saw. Fixed in 2.1.221.

slides.title: Worktrees were not isolated
slides.sub: Isolated sessions and their subagents could still run destructive git against the main checkout. Fixed in 2.1.222.

slides.title: One trailing slash
slides.sub: denyRead "~/.aws/" was silently bypassable on Linux and macOS. Drop the slash. Fixed in 2.1.224.

slides.title: Do this today
items: Grep settings for denyRead and denyWrite trailing slashes
Audit every PreToolUse hook that auto-allows a tool
Sandbox denials now surface in Bash results. Read them.
